pattern.crimePattern: a mother who has watched the road for nine years kills the lorry driver she learns ran over her son, and stages a brake failure on the bend
pattern.notes: Fictional people, bend and transporters. The child's death nine years ago is told only in a closed police file, in report language, and never shown. "Bandits" is the story everyone reaches for; the evidence clears them (region rule). Open decision for the user: the child death in the back-story (see the region report).

ob.text: A bus crew reports a lorry gone off the road at the Bakuli bend on the descent from Marsabit mountain, the driver dead in the cab: Kirimi Mbaabu (54). Talk in town says bandits stopped him.

reconstruction.text: Nine years ago, at dusk, a lorry hits Aliyo's son Lokho as he crosses the Bakuli bend with the family's goats, and drives on. The file is closed: "unknown vehicle". A year later she opens a tea kiosk at the bend and watches every lorry.
In March she sees an old photo on the Marsabit noticeboard: Kirimi's red lorry with a dented bumper, and an invoice for the repair dated the day after Lokho died.
Wednesday, 19:05. Kirimi passes Logologo alone; he dropped his turnboy in town. At 20:31 he stops for tea at her kiosk and calls his wife.
She asks him about the dent. He laughs: children should keep off the road. As he turns to his cab she strikes him with the brazier poker, pushes him into the driver's seat and lets off the handbrake.
The lorry rolls 60 metres and over the bend. At 20:52 she calls her husband: "It's done. Lokho can rest." In the morning she tells the bus crew she heard brakes and bandits.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on both lines and a warrant on the kiosk. Detain Aliyo after the search; the poker trace (12 h + 4) and the tread (8 h + 4) come back inside 24 h. The post-mortem in Marsabit runs in parallel.

ui.beatNotes: Two files at once. When the old file is found, Lokho's thin closed folder slides onto the desk beside the live case. Evidence can be dragged between them; the dent invoice belongs to both. The verdict stamps both.
